title: Return the next slice body in one call to cut a model round trip
lead:
The agent loop forces two turns to begin work: `next --json` to get the id, then
`show ID --json` to read the slice. Every turn replays the whole growing context,
so that second turn is the most expensive unit in the flow. `next --start` already
proves the "fuse two steps into one call" pattern; the read half is still split.
Add `--show` so `next` (and `next --start`) returns the item together with the slice
sections, boundary, and dependencies in one payload, removing a full model turn per
slice picked up.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
A driving agent cannot implement from `next` alone — it always follows with `show`.
Because each command is a separate model turn and each turn re-sends the entire
context, collapsing `next`+`show` into one call saves far more than trimming bytes.
This is the single highest-leverage credit optimization in the agent flow.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
`src/slicer/cli.py` (the `next` subcommand and its `--start` handling),
`src/slicer/ops.py` (assemble item + slice payload), `docs/agents.md` and
`src/slicer/ai.py` (document the one-call loop).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Add `--show` to `next`. When set, include the item's `slice` object (the same shape
`show ID --json` returns: lead, sections, boundary, depends) in the payload. Compose
with `--start` and `--render` so `next --start --show --json` returns the started
item and everything needed to implement it. Keep the default `next` output unchanged.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
`next --start --show --json` returns the started item plus its full `slice` in one
invocation, byte-identical to what `show ID --json` would have returned separately.
A test asserts the fused payload equals the two-call composition. `--json` contract
codes are unchanged. `docs/agents.md` and `ai instructions` describe the one-call loop.
